explanation: Work is energy transferred when a force pushes something through a distance, but ONLY the part of the force that lies ALONG the motion counts — that is the cos θ. Slide the force F (red arrow) and the displacement d (green arrow); the block slides back and forth so you can watch them. Tilt the angle θ to 0° and all the force does work; tilt it to 90° (straight up) and the force does ZERO work, no matter how strong, because it never moves the block forward.
bullets: Only the force component along the displacement does work: W = F·d·cos θ.
θ = 0° gives maximum work; θ = 90° gives zero work (force ⟂ motion).
Work is measured in joules (1 J = 1 N·m); θ > 90° makes W negative.
